text: Investigating now. Plan: make dayjs.tz() treat non-string inputs (Date, timestamp, Day.js object) as an instant and convert it to the target zone, instead of re-parsing it as wall-clock time. ETA ~15 min.

Investigating now. The offset is computed from a locale-string round trip that drops milliseconds, leaving a fractional minute offset. Plan: round the computed minute difference so the offset is a clean whole minute. ETA ~15 min.
Investigating now. Plan: give the nl locale a proper ordinal function that picks 'ste' for 1, 8 and >= 20 and 'de' otherwise (1ste, 8ste, 19de, 20ste). ETA ~15 min.
Looking at the weekYear plugin now (en-gb sets yearStart: 4, which the plugin appears to ignore). ETA ~14 min.
Looking at the customParseFormat plugin's meridiem (A/a) handling with the zh-cn locale. ETA ~14 min.
Looking at the duration plugin's unit parsing for 'ms'. ETA ~14 min.

Fixed and verified: dayjs.tz() now treats a Date / timestamp / Day.js object as an absolute instant and converts it to the target zone (dayjs.tz(new Date('2020-08-07T12:00-07:00'), 'America/Vancouver').format() === '2020-08-07T12:00:00-07:00'), while strings keep their wall-clock meaning.

Fixed and verified: the minute difference is now rounded, so dayjs('2020-08-06T03:48:10.258Z').tz('Asia/Tokyo').format('Z') === '+09:00' (utcOffset 540), and the milliseconds of the instant are carried over so valueOf() stays exact (1596685690258).

Fixed: the nl locale now picks the Dutch ordinal suffix by number — 1ste, 2de, 8ste, 19de, 20ste, 31ste — so dayjs('2018-05-08').locale('nl').format('Do') === '8ste' and dayjs('2018-05-19').locale('nl').format('Do') === '19de'.
